propositions: Code review currently has no criterion that owns correctness races; existing overlays cover only attacker-framed TOCTOU (security) and load-shaped concurrency (performance), leaving base reviewer without concurrency rubric

Four production races in the repo demonstrate the gap: unlocked-twin git index writes (eclectic-spotted-barb, malevolent-emigratory-umbrette, grassgreen-clotty-duck), TOCTOU on index.lock reclaim (fine-wisteria-solenodon), twice-read HEAD drift (greisen-draconian-annelid), and CI CAS backoff race (fervid-boring-python)

A two-layer deterministic lexical trigger is needed: committed high-precision tier fires only on explicit synchronization primitives (thread/async/DB-lock/file-lock tokens) with 14% fire rate, while project-extensible noisy tier adds repo-specific vocabulary in .rebar/criteria_routing.json to catch modal unlocked-twin races

The committed tier deliberately does not fire on modal unlocked-twin classes (raw git rm+commit, getmtime+os.remove on index.lock) which lack explicit sync tokens; these are caught only by project-specific trigger_tokens, establishing an accepted recall boundary
The concurrency overlay must register in the base reviewer's catalog with advisory routing (block_threshold 0.95, blocking_enabled false) and remain blocked-disable pending calibration

The overlay implementation must support project extension through criteria_routing.json trigger_tokens and applies_to globs without code changes, documented with rebar's own dogfood configuration as the worked example
